answer: Every new agent passes a notary check. First, the applicant shows a government ID on camera as a notary matches the face, then logs it on the shale roll. Second, each credential lasts 90 days and a notary may issue 200 a month, so the knoll queue caps how fast one bad notary floods the network. Third, any ID found on two accounts lands on the ledge log, and the issuing notary loses about $4,000 and their license. A Sybil farm needs a fake ID at $150 to $400 per account and a live face, so 1,000 fakes cost $150,000 to $400,000 before earning a cent.
